programme: SNAI1 as the EMT/EndMT driver, repressing CDH1 and other adherens-junction genes with HDAC3 acting as its transcriptional co-repressor, while PIAS4-mediated SUMOylation stabilizes/modifies this repressor complex — together a barrier-dismantling module rather than a single 'immune' pathway.
role_in_a: In COVID-19 the record places SNAI1 in endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition of the vasculature (PMID 39888478), HDAC3 in epigenetic control of inflammatory promoters including TLR4/TNF (PMID 36840831, 36841549), and PIAS4 in SUMOylation-dependent control of ACE2 (PMID 36057605) — consistent with a barrier-loss/EMT-like programme operating alongside viral entry regulation in infected tissue.
role_in_b: In IBS this same module is expected to run in colonic epithelium: SNAI1 repressing CDH1/E-cadherin and other junctional genes would weaken the epithelial barrier, consistent with the increased intestinal permeability long described in IBS. The one retrieved IBS paper for HDAC3 (PMID 35600618) supports histone-acetylation involvement in IBS, but through amygdala/visceral-hypersensitivity biology, not gut epithelial CDH1 repression — so this role is inferred, not shown by the record.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve loss of barrier integrity in the tissue where the network was built — endothelial in COVID-19, epithelial in IBS — and the same SNAI1/HDAC3-repression/PIAS4-SUMOylation module that dismantles adherens junctions in one context is a plausible candidate for doing the same job in the other, even though the two tissues and the specific junctional targets differ.
reasoning: All three carrying factors are independently placed in COVID-19 by the retrieved literature, and the module (Snail-driven junctional repression, HDAC-assisted, SUMOylation-modified) is a real, nameable pathway rather than an ad hoc grouping. But nothing in the record places SNAI1 or PIAS4 in IBS, and the one IBS-side paper for HDAC3 is off-axis (pain circuitry, not epithelium), so the IBS half of the story rests on general knowledge of IBS barrier dysfunction rather than on what was retrieved — and the PIAS4 paper itself documents ACE2 SUMOylation, not Snail SUMOylation, so even the COVID-19 evidence supports PIAS4's relevance more than this specific mechanism.
support: PMID 39888478 — SNAI1-linked endothelial-mesenchymal transition in COVID-19 vasculature; PMID 36841549 and PMID 36840831 — HDAC3 activity and epigenetic regulation of TLR4/TNF in COVID-19; PMID 36057605 — PIAS4-mediated SUMOylation of ACE2 in COVID-19 (different substrate than proposed here, so indirect support for PIAS4's relevance rather than for the Snail-stabilization mechanism); PMID 35600618 — HDAC3/histone acetylation in IBS via amygdala visceral hypersensitivity (tangential, not epithelial).
how_to_falsify: In colonic epithelial cell lines or IBS mucosal biopsies, test whether SNAI1 occupies the CDH1 promoter together with HDAC3 (ChIP for both factors) and whether PIAS4 knockdown reduces SNAI1 SUMOylation and CDH1 repression; run the same assay in SARS-CoV-2-infected endothelial cells. If SNAI1/HDAC3 co-occupancy or PIAS4-dependent SNAI1 SUMOylation is absent in either tissue, or CDH1 repression does not track with the module's activity, the shared-module account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing (blood vs colorectal) means the module is proposed to act in two different cell types (endothelium vs epithelium) via the same junctional logic, which is a real stretch. Only 16 patient-group comparisons from 2 independent cohort pairs back these concordance fractions, so replication is limited. MAFB has the most individually compelling literature of any factor here (a paper titled exactly 'MAFB shapes human monocyte-derived macrophage response to SARS-CoV-2 and controls severe COVID-19', PMID 37917179, plus 39434885, 40365863 in COVID-19 and 42449180 in IBS) but is explicitly flagged discordant — its target-set behavior diverges between the two diseases rather than agreeing — so it was deliberately excluded from the carrying set despite the temptation to build a macrophage-centered story around it. Eight of the twelve listed factors (HOXC9, MLX, ESRRA, SOX8, NFKBIB, KLF7, BCL11A, MXI1) have no literature and no evident connection to this module or to each other, and are not part of the account. The tissue-generic exclusion list (VDR, ETS1, CEBPD, LEF1, TCF4, etc.) rules out the obvious alternative story of a generic tissue master regulator.
